name: Arrochar
intro: Arrochar is a Staten Island neighborhood. The Arrochar Older Adult Center on Bionia Avenue is run by Staten Island Friendship Clubs under contract with NYC Aging. The South Beach Library serves the South Beach and Arrochar communities.

seniorCenter.name: Arrochar Older Adult Center (Staten Island Friendship Clubs)
seniorCenter.notes: Run by Staten Island Friendship Clubs under contract with NYC Aging. Open Monday to Friday, 8 am to 4 pm. Breakfast is served at 8:30 am and lunch at noon, cooked fresh on site, with grab-and-go meals for pickup. The clubs offer door-to-door transportation, blood pressure screenings, falls prevention and tai chi for arthritis classes, and chair exercise. NYC Aging older adult center membership is free for New Yorkers 60 and older.

transport.name: Access-A-Ride (MTA paratransit)
transport.notes: Shared-ride service for people whose disabilities keep them from using buses or the subway. It runs 24 hours a day, every day, including holidays, in all five boroughs. Press 2 to book a trip one to two days ahead (agents 7 am to 5 pm, every day), or press 4 for eligibility and application questions (9 am to 5 pm, Monday to Friday). Anyone 65 or older can also get the MTA Reduced Fare, $1.50 a ride on the subway, local buses and the Staten Island Railway.

library.address: 41 Father Capodanno Boulevard, Staten Island, NY 10305
library.notes: Fully accessible, with books and films in Russian, Chinese and Spanish. Check the branch page for this week's hours. The New York Public Library no longer charges late fines.

name: Bedford
intro: Bedford is a town in Westchester County. Its Recreation and Parks Department runs senior adult meetings and programs with free local rides for shopping and meetings, a senior advocate for residents and their families, and lunch and Meals on Wheels through an agreement with the Village of Mount Kisco.

seniorCenter.name: Town of Bedford Senior Adults (Recreation and Parks)
seniorCenter.notes: Senior adults meet regularly for talks, crafts, exercise, movies, parties and special programs. Call the Seniors Line to join the mailing list for the bimonthly calendar. The town's senior advocate helps all Bedford residents, including family members who live outside the town, with aging-related resources, caregiver support groups and help for people with movement or vision difficulties. A senior nutrition program and home-delivered Meals on Wheels are offered through an agreement with the Village of Mount Kisco.

transport.name: Town of Bedford senior bus
transport.notes: Free rides from Recreation and Parks for local shopping and senior meetings. Call the Seniors Line for the schedule. Bee-Line ParaTransit (914-995-7272) serves people who cannot ride regular buses, for a $5 fare.

more.name: Town of Bedford Senior Advocate
more.note: Free help for Bedford residents and their immediate family members, including those who live outside the town, with aging-related resources, caregiver support groups and grant information.

more.name: Town of Bedford Recreation and Parks office
more.note: 425 Cherry Street, Bedford Hills. Open Monday to Friday, 8:30 am to 4:30 pm.

name: Blooming Grove
intro: Blooming Grove is a town in Orange County that includes the villages of Washingtonville and South Blooming Grove. The town's Senior and Nutrition Center serves a county lunch three days a week, and a town senior bus takes residents over 60 shopping in Monroe and Vails Gate.

seniorCenter.name: Blooming Grove Senior and Nutrition Center
seniorCenter.notes: Lunch is served at noon three days a week for people 60 and older, including Tuesdays and Fridays. Call ahead to reserve and to confirm the days. There is no fee, and a $3.50 contribution per meal is suggested. The weekly schedule includes a painting club, movie afternoons, mahjong, card games and bingo. Home delivered meals need a prescreening and an in-home assessment; call the county Office for the Aging at 845-615-3700.

transport.name: Blooming Grove Senior Bus
transport.notes: For town residents over 60, including Washingtonville and South Blooming Grove. The bus picks you up at home and goes to Monroe area stores and Woodbury Commons on Wednesdays and Fridays, and to Vails Gate and Newburgh shopping on Thursdays. A $1 donation is requested each way. Call Monday to Friday at least 24 hours ahead. Trips may be canceled if few people sign up.

library.name: Moffat Library of Washingtonville
library.notes: The library and its drive-thru window are open Monday to Thursday 10 am to 8 pm, Friday 10 am to 6 pm, Saturday 10 am to 5 pm and Sunday noon to 5 pm. The library has a home delivery service.

name: Brewster
intro: Brewster is a village in Putnam County with a Metro-North Harlem Line station. The Brewster Public Library is on Main Street, a five-minute walk from the train station. PART Route 1 runs from Brewster to Putnam Lake and meets Metro-North at the Brewster station.

transport.name: PART Route 1 (Brewster and Putnam Lake)
transport.notes: PART Route 1 runs from Brewster to Putnam Lake by way of Brewster Village, Brewster Hill, Lakeview Plaza and Doansburg Road, with stops at downtown Brewster and the Brewster Metro-North station. Buses stop anywhere along the route when you flag them. The regular fare is $2.50. Riders 65 and older and disabled riders pay $1.25 by showing an Office for Senior Resources ID, a Medicare card, an MTA disability card or a county Half-Fare card. Exact change is needed. Buses run Monday to Friday 4:50 am to 8 pm and Saturday 8 am to 6 pm, with no Sunday service.

library.name: Brewster Public Library
library.notes: Open Monday to Thursday 9 am to 7 pm, Friday 9 am to 4 pm and Saturday 10 am to 3 pm. A five-minute walk from the Brewster Metro-North station, with metered parking on Main Street.

more.name: Putnam County Office for Senior Resources
more.note: Main line for NY Connects, HIICAP Medicare counseling, EPIC help, home care, home delivered meals, caregiver support and a legal consultation with an attorney by appointment. The office also certifies HEAP heating aid applications for residents 60 and older. Donald B. Smith Campus, 110 Old Route 6, Building 3, Carmel.

more.name: Office for Senior Resources medical transportation
more.note: Limited rides to doctor and hospital appointments for older residents with no other way to get there, driven by Putnam SeniorCorps volunteers. Rides go within Putnam County and to certain places outside it.

more.name: PART Paratransit
more.note: Origin-to-destination vans for residents whose disability keeps them off the regular PART bus, within 3/4 mile of a PART route. Age alone does not qualify. A one-way trip is $3.25 and an attendant rides free. Call 845-878-3480 for an application, which takes up to 21 days to process.

name: Briarcliff Manor
intro: Briarcliff Manor is a village in Westchester County. The Town of Ossining's senior center extends home-delivered lunches and discount taxi coupons to Briarcliff seniors, and the public library sits in Law Park on Library Road.

transport.name: Ossining Senior Center taxi coupons
transport.notes: Discount taxi coupons for Ossining and Briarcliff seniors 60 and older cost $3 each, up to 15 a month, with proof of age and residency. They can be used in and around Ossining, Briarcliff, the Croton ShopRite and Phelps Hospital only. Bee-Line ParaTransit (914-995-7272) serves people who cannot ride regular buses.

library.name: Briarcliff Manor Public Library
library.notes: Housed in a 2008 addition to a historic train station in Law Park. Open Monday to Wednesday, Friday and Saturday 10 am to 5 pm, Thursday 10 am to 7 pm, and closed Sunday.

sources: Westchester County DOT: ParaTransit Quick Reference

more.name: Ossining Senior Center home-delivered meals
more.note: The center at 95 Broadway, Ossining, delivers a hot lunch Monday to Friday to qualifying homebound seniors in Ossining and Briarcliff, for a $3.50 suggested contribution. Call for program guidelines.

name: Bronxville
intro: Bronxville is a village in the Town of Eastchester. Older residents can use Eastchester Senior Programs and Services, including medical rides and the senior center at Lake Isle, and the Bronxville Senior Citizens club meets twice a week at the Reformed Church on Pondfield Road.

seniorCenter.name: Bronxville Senior Citizens
seniorCenter.address: The Reformed Church of Bronxville, 180 Pondfield Road, Bronxville, NY 10708
seniorCenter.notes: A club for people 55 and older, run by the nonprofit Senior Citizens Council with support from the Town of Eastchester. It meets Tuesdays and Thursdays, September through July, and is closed in August. Membership is open to all who consider Bronxville their community; dues are $175 a year ($87.50 for members 90 and older). Programs include exercise, chair yoga, tai chi, line dancing, bridge, mah-jongg, canasta and talks; luncheons and day trips cost extra. Bronxville residents 60 and older can also use the Town of Eastchester's Center at Lake Isle (660 White Plains Road, 914-337-0390), which serves lunch daily and offers rides to residents of Eastchester, Tuckahoe and Bronxville. The county lists the lunch site as temporarily at the Tuckahoe Community Center, 71 Columbus Avenue, so call to confirm where lunch is served.

transport.name: Eastchester Senior Programs medical rides
transport.notes: Rides to medical appointments for residents 60 and older of Eastchester, Tuckahoe and Bronxville, Monday to Friday, 9 am to 2 pm, by reservation. A free escort gives light help when needed. Suggested round trip contributions are voluntary, at $5 within Eastchester, Tuckahoe, Bronxville and Scarsdale Village, $8 to Scarsdale, Mount Vernon, New Rochelle and Yonkers, and $10 to White Plains, Hartsdale and Harrison. The town also offers shopping and errand rides. Bee-Line ParaTransit (914-995-7272) serves people who cannot ride regular buses.

library.notes: The library lists resources for people with low vision.

name: Carmel
intro: Carmel is home to the Putnam County Office for Senior Resources on the Donald B. Smith Campus, where the Carmel Friendship Center serves a hot lunch on weekdays. PART Route 5 runs from Carmel to Lake Carmel, and Putnam On-Demand shared rides reach parts of the Town of Carmel.

seniorCenter.name: Carmel Friendship Center
seniorCenter.notes: Run by the Putnam County Office for Senior Resources. Hot noontime lunch is served Monday to Friday, except holidays and days the center closes for training or weather. Programs include exercise, fall prevention classes such as A Matter of Balance and Tai Chi for Arthritis, blood pressure readings, arts and crafts, games and talks by local doctors and pharmacists. Transportation and shopping help are offered to people with no other way to get there. Call the Office for Senior Resources to take part.

transport.name: PART Route 5 (Carmel and Lake Carmel)
transport.notes: PART Route 5 runs from Carmel to Lake Carmel by way of Carmel Plaza and Kent, with stops at Reed Memorial Library and the Putnam County offices. Buses stop anywhere along the route when you flag them. The regular fare is $2.50. Riders 65 and older and disabled riders pay $1.25 by showing an Office for Senior Resources ID, a Medicare card, an MTA disability card or a county Half-Fare card. Exact change is needed. Buses run Monday to Friday 4:50 am to 8 pm and Saturday 8 am to 6 pm, with no Sunday service. PART Route 2 serves Mahopac. Putnam On-Demand shared rides cover the Town of Patterson and parts of the Towns of Carmel and Southeast, Monday to Friday 8 am to 6 pm and Saturday 9 am to 3 pm, for $1.25 a ride for seniors. Book in the app or at 845-475-0557. Drivers do not take cash.

library.name: Reed Memorial Library
library.notes: Open Monday, Wednesday and Friday 10 am to 5 pm, Tuesday and Thursday 10 am to 7 pm, and Saturday 10 am to 1 pm. Closed Sundays. Some programs and hold pickups happen at the RML Community Hub, 9 Church Street, with free on-street parking on Seminary Hill Road.

more.name: Carmel and Mahopac outreach (Office for Senior Resources)
more.note: Outreach staff help isolated older residents get services and apply or recertify for Medicaid, SNAP and the Medicare Savings Program.

more.name: William Koehler Memorial Senior Center
more.note: 180 Route 6, Mahopac. A county senior center with a weekday lunch and the SOAP shower and laundry program.

intro: Chelsea is on Manhattan's West Side. Hudson Guild, established in 1895 and rooted in Chelsea, runs an older adult center at its Fulton Community Center on Ninth Avenue. The Muhlenberg Library on West 23rd Street has served Chelsea since 1906.

seniorCenter.notes: Breakfast and lunch are served Monday to Friday for people 60 and older, with about 60 activities such as yoga, tai chi, painting and sewing. Hudson Guild's Social Services Unit offers counseling, help applying for benefits, free legal assistance, financial coaching, a health insurance advocate, MetroCard mobile services and tenant help. Staff speak Spanish, Cantonese and Mandarin as well as English. NYC Aging older adult center membership is free for New Yorkers 60 and older.

intro: Chester is a town in Orange County that includes the Village of Chester and the hamlet of Sugar Loaf, with Town Hall at 1786 Kings Highway. The Town of Chester Senior Center is the hub for residents 60 and older, with exercise classes, games and a county senior lunch twice a week, and a Dial-A-Ride bus serves Chester and Goshen.

seniorCenter.name: Town of Chester Senior Center
seniorCenter.notes: For residents 60 and older. Weekly programs include gentle stretch and exercise, chair yoga, mat yoga, tai chi, quilting, mahjong and open cards and games. Fitness classes cost $10 a month for residents 60 and older, and tai chi is $20 a month. The Orange County Office for the Aging serves a Senior Dining lunch here on Tuesdays and Thursdays around 11:30 am for people 60 and older. There is no fee, a $3.50 contribution is suggested, and you must reserve 24 hours ahead at 845-469-7000 option 3 or by text at 845-325-7227.

transport.name: Goshen and Chester Dial-A-Ride
transport.notes: Curb-to-curb rides that must start in the Town of Goshen or the Town of Chester, to anywhere in those two towns. The bus runs Monday to Friday 8 am to 5 pm. The senior fare is $2. Call 8 am to noon on weekdays, at least 24 hours and up to a week ahead.

more.name: Town of Chester
more.note: Town Hall at 1786 Kings Highway is open Monday to Friday 8 am to 5 pm.

more.name: Orange County Office for the Aging
more.note: Aging Services Specialists answer questions about county services for older adults and can arrange home visits for homebound seniors. Bilingual help is available.

name: Clarkstown
intro: Clarkstown is a town in Rockland County, with Town Hall at 10 Maple Avenue in New City. Its communities include New City, Nanuet, Congers, West Nyack and Bardonia. Older residents can join nine town senior clubs, ride the town Mini Trans bus at a reduced fare, and get lunch at the Meals on Wheels center in Nanuet.

seniorCenter.name: Clarkstown/Pearl River Senior Activity Center (Meals on Wheels Rockland)
seniorCenter.notes: Free to join for Rockland residents 60 and older. Open Monday to Friday, 10 am to 2 pm, and closed on holidays and bad weather days. Lunch is made daily, with kosher, therapeutic and mechanically altered choices. The suggested donation is $4 for lunch and $2 for a ride, and no one is refused service for not giving. Call or fill out the center's online form to join.

transport.name: Clarkstown Mini Trans
transport.notes: The town bus runs five routes that all meet at the Nanuet Mall. It runs Monday to Friday 6:55 am to 8:05 pm and Saturday 9 am to 7:10 pm, with no Sunday service. The senior and disabled fare is $0.40. It also gives weekday door-to-door rides to the Clarkstown senior clubs and rides from senior complexes to local supermarkets.

library.name: New City Library
library.address: 220 N. Main Street, New City, NY 10956
library.notes: One of several public libraries in the town. Nanuet and West Nyack have their own.

more.name: Clarkstown Senior Citizen Clubs
more.note: Nine town clubs for Clarkstown residents 55 and older meet weekly in Congers, Nanuet, New City and West Nyack. A free Senior ID card, good for five years, is needed to use town community centers, pools and the Stay Fit program. The phone is the town's main line.

more.name: Stay Fit Seniors (Clarkstown Parks and Recreation)
more.note: A 30-minute circuit wellness program for people 60 and older at the Street Community Center in New City. You must sign up ahead.

more.name: Town of Clarkstown Assessor
more.note: Call with questions about property tax exemptions for older homeowners.

more.name: TRIPS Paratransit (Rockland County)
more.note: County shared-ride bus for residents 60 and older who find the regular buses hard to use. For help applying, the county lists 845-364-2065.

places.note: At 299 Rockland Lake Road in Valley Cottage. A 3.2-mile paved trail for walkers and cyclists circles the lake, and the park has picnic areas with tables. Open year round, daylight to dusk; a $10 vehicle fee is collected on spring and fall weekends and holidays and every day in summer.

seniorCenter.notes: Run by the Putnam County Office for Senior Resources. Hot noontime lunch is served Monday to Friday, except holidays and days the center closes for training or weather. Programs include exercise, fall prevention classes such as A Matter of Balance and Tai Chi for Arthritis, blood pressure readings, arts and crafts, games and talks by local doctors and pharmacists. Morabito Community Center in Cortlandt Manor for town residents 60 and older, with lunch, a weekday bus and senior clubs.

intro: Crawford is a town in Orange County that includes the hamlet of Pine Bush. The Pine Bush Seniors club for people 55 and older meets every Tuesday at the Town of Crawford Community Center on Route 302, and the Town of Montgomery's Senior Bus and Dial-A-Bus also serve Crawford.

seniorCenter.name: Town of Crawford Community Center (Pine Bush Seniors)
seniorCenter.notes: The Pine Bush Seniors welcome everyone 55 and older. Meetings are on Tuesdays. Doors open at 11 am for social time, with a short business meeting at 12:15 pm. Your first three meetings are free, then dues are $2 a meeting, and members 90 and older pay nothing. Meetings include bingo, speakers and holiday luncheons, and the club runs bus trips. No meeting when Pine Bush schools are closed or have a two-hour weather delay.

transport.name: Town of Montgomery Senior Bus and Dial-A-Bus
transport.notes: Both buses run in the towns of Montgomery and Crawford, including Pine Bush, Thompson Ridge, Bullville and Searsville. name: Mahopac
intro: Mahopac is home to Putnam County's William Koehler Memorial Senior Center on Route 6, which serves a hot weekday lunch and offers walk-in shower and laundry help. PART Route 2 links Mahopac with the Jefferson Valley Mall and stops at the Koehler Center.

seniorCenter.name: William Koehler Memorial Senior Center
seniorCenter.notes: Run by the Putnam County Office for Senior Resources. Hot noontime lunch is served Monday to Friday, except holidays and days the center closes for training or weather. Programs include exercise, fall prevention classes such as A Matter of Balance and Tai Chi for Arthritis, blood pressure readings, arts and crafts, games and talks by local doctors and pharmacists. Transportation and shopping help are offered to people with no other way to get there. Call the Office for Senior Resources to take part. This center also has walk-in shower and laundry help with a certified aide (the SOAP program), after a case manager's assessment.

transport.name: PART Route 2 (Mahopac and Jefferson Valley)
transport.notes: PART Route 2 runs between Mahopac and the Jefferson Valley Mall by way of Lake Plaza, downtown Mahopac, Somers Commons, Baldwin Place and Mahopac Falls, with a stop at the Koehler Center (not on snow routes). Buses stop anywhere along the route when you flag them. The regular fare is $2.50. Riders 65 and older and disabled riders pay $1.25 by showing an Office for Senior Resources ID, a Medicare card, an MTA disability card or a county Half-Fare card. Exact change is needed. Buses run Monday to Friday 4:50 am to 8 pm and Saturday 8 am to 6 pm, with no Sunday service. A weekday shuttle from Mahopac, with a stop at Mahopac Library, meets Metro-North trains at Croton Falls for $1 a trip.

library.name: Mahopac Public Library
library.notes: Open Monday to Thursday 9:30 am to 8 pm, Friday 9:30 am to 7 pm, Saturday 9:30 am to 3 pm and Sunday 1 to 5 pm. Mahopac residents 14 and older can apply for a card online.

more.name: Carmel and Mahopac outreach (Office for Senior Resources)
more.note: Outreach staff help isolated older residents get services and apply or recertify for Medicaid, SNAP and the Medicare Savings Program.

more.name: Putnam County Office for Senior Resources
more.note: Main line for NY Connects, HIICAP Medicare counseling, EPIC help, home care, home delivered meals, caregiver support and a legal consultation with an attorney by appointment. more.name: Office for Senior Resources medical transportation
more.note: Limited rides to doctor and hospital appointments for older residents with no other way to get there, driven by Putnam SeniorCorps volunteers. Rides go within Putnam County and to certain places outside it.

more.name: PART Paratransit
more.note: Origin-to-destination vans for residents whose disability keeps them off the regular PART bus, within 3/4 mile of a PART route. Age alone does not qualify. A one-way trip is $3.25 and an attendant rides free. Call 845-878-3480 for an application, which takes up to 21 days to process.

Its senior center on Boston Post Road in Larchmont serves adults 55 and older with classes, events, a weekday lunch and rides, and people who live in the town, the Village of Larchmont or the Village of Mamaroneck pay the resident rate.

seniorCenter.notes: Run by the Town of Mamaroneck Recreation Department at VFW David Potts Jr. Post #1156, for adults 55 and older. Open year round, Monday to Friday. Services include exercise classes, games, lectures, art classes, monthly events, rides to medical appointments and to the center, grocery shopping and Meals on Wheels. A hot lunch is served weekdays at noon; reserve at least two days ahead by calling between 9 am and 2 pm. The suggested contribution is $4, and people under 60 pay the full $9 cost.

Middletown Area Transit buses give a reduced fare to seniors and Medicare card holders.

Offerings include exercise, yoga, art, theater, crafts and music, an AARP Smart Driving course, tax-aide and e-filing, a computer lab with classes, and help with health insurance problems and Food Stamps (SNAP) applications. transport.notes: Door-to-door rides for people 60 and older who live in the City of Middletown. It runs Monday to Friday 8:30 am to 4:30 pm and Sunday 8 am to 12:30 pm, for a suggested donation of $1 per ride.

seniorCenter.notes: Open to Town of Monroe residents 60 and older; bring proof of residency such as a tax bill or a current utility bill. Classes include yoga, stretch, chair aerobics and balance work, and there is Thursday bingo, a computer lab, card games and a free blood pressure screening on the second Thursday of the month. Two senior clubs meet here twice a month (yearly dues are $15 and $12) and plan trips. An AARP defensive driving class runs in spring and late fall.

transport.notes: Rides in the Town of Monroe and the villages of Monroe and Harriman, with limited trips to parts of Kiryas Joel and Woodbury. Seniors 55 and older pay $1 with proof of age, exact change only. Phones are answered Monday to Friday 8 am to 3:30 pm. Book at least three days ahead if you can, and no more than one week ahead. Give 24 hours notice to cancel.

intro: Newburgh is a city in Orange County, separate from the Town of Newburgh. Newburgh Area Transit buses run every 30 minutes on Broadway and reach St. Luke's and Cornwall hospitals and Vails Gate shopping for a $0.75 senior fare, and the Newburgh Free Library on Grand Street offers home delivery.

transport.notes: Wheelchair accessible local routes in the city that extend into the towns of Newburgh and New Windsor, with stops at St. Luke's Hospital, Cornwall Hospital, Mount Saint Mary College, the Newburgh Mall and Vails Gate stores. library.notes: Open September to June Monday to Thursday 9 am to 8 pm, Friday and Saturday 9 am to 5 pm and Sunday 1 to 5 pm, with shorter summer hours. The library offers homebound delivery for those who qualify, curbside pickup, and free computer classes and one-on-one tech help.

intro: North Salem is a town in Westchester County. The North Salem Community Center in Croton Falls doubles as the senior center, the town runs a door to door senior van for residents 60 and older, and home-delivered meals come through a partnership with the Town of Somers.

seniorCenter.name: North Salem Community Center and Senior Center
seniorCenter.notes: Open to residents weekdays, 9 am to 4:30 pm, with a lounge, Wi-Fi, TV, games, puzzles, books, coffee and snacks, plus free fitness, craft and educational programs. transport.name: North Salem Senior Van
transport.notes: A new town van gives door to door rides to residents 60 and older for local shopping and programs. Contact the Recreation Department to book. F.I.S.H. Bee-Line ParaTransit (914-995-7272) serves people who cannot ride regular buses.

more.name: Somers-North Salem-Lewisboro Nutrition Program (home-delivered meals)
more.note: A hot weekday lunch delivered to residents 60 and older who need help for health reasons. Suggested donation $3 per meal.

name: Ossining
intro: Ossining is a town in Westchester County. The town's Senior Services department, at the Joseph G. Caputo Community Center on Broadway, is open to all Town of Ossining residents 60 and older, with a weekday lunch, home-delivered meals, a daily check-in call, a grocery bus and discount taxi coupons.

seniorCenter.notes: Office hours are Monday to Friday, 8 am to 3 pm, and the center is handicapped accessible. Hot lunches are delivered weekdays to qualifying homebound seniors in Ossining and Briarcliff ($3.50 suggested). The RUOK (Are You Okay?) program makes a check-in call every morning, 7 days a week. A social worker is at the center 8:30 am to 1:30 pm for information and referrals (914-762-7655). Weekly classes include Stay Strong and Fit, chair yoga and line dancing. The center closes when Ossining Public Schools close for weather.

transport.notes: A bus goes to the Croton ShopRite every Wednesday at 12:30 pm for seniors who eat lunch at the center first, then drives them home; the fee is $2 and you must reserve. Discount taxi coupons for Ossining and Briarcliff residents 60 and older cost $3 each, up to 15 a month, with proof of age and residency. They can be used in and around the Town and Village of Ossining, Briarcliff, the Croton ShopRite and Phelps Hospital only. name: Pelham
intro: Pelham is a town in Westchester County. Town programs are open to residents 55 and older at the Daronco Town House on Fifth Avenue, including a weekly senior club, exercise and yoga classes, card games and a medical van.

seniorCenter.name: Daronco Town House (Town of Pelham senior programs)
seniorCenter.notes: For Town of Pelham residents 55 and older. The Senior Citizen Club meets Mondays, 1 to 4 pm, with bingo, meetings and special events, and collects small monthly dues. Senior exercise runs Tuesday and Thursday at 10 am, yoga for seniors Friday at 10 am, and cards (bridge, mah-jongg and more) Wednesday and Friday afternoons. The Resident Emergency Assistance List (R.E.A.L.), run with the Pelham and Pelham Manor police, lets older residents sign up for check-ins during storms and power outages.

transport.name: Town of Pelham medical van
transport.notes: Medical trips only, Monday to Thursday, with the first pickup at 9:15 am and the last at 3 pm. Book 24 hours ahead. Riders sit in the back and must get in and out without help. Service covers Pelham, New Rochelle, Larchmont, Eastchester, Bronxville, Mount Vernon, part of Scarsdale and the Ridge Hill area of Yonkers. Bee-Line ParaTransit (914-995-7272) serves people who need more help.

library.name: Town of Pelham Public Library
library.notes: Open Monday and Thursday 10 am to 8 pm, Tuesday, Wednesday and Friday 10 am to 5 pm, and Saturday 10 am to 4 pm.

name: Philipstown
intro: Philipstown is a town in Putnam County. The county's Friendship Center in Philipstown, at 6 Butterfield Road in Cold Spring, serves a hot weekday lunch. The Desmond-Fish Public Library in Garrison serves Philipstown residents and is open seven days a week.

seniorCenter.name: Friendship Center in Philipstown
seniorCenter.notes: Run by the Putnam County Office for Senior Resources. Hot noontime lunch is served Monday to Friday, except holidays and days the center closes for training or weather. Programs include exercise, fall prevention classes such as A Matter of Balance and Tai Chi for Arthritis, blood pressure readings, arts and crafts, games and talks by local doctors and pharmacists. Transportation and shopping help are offered to people with no other way to get there. Call the center or the main office at 845-808-1700 to take part.

transport.name: Office for Senior Resources medical transportation
transport.notes: Limited rides to doctor and hospital appointments for older residents with no other way to get there, driven by Putnam SeniorCorps volunteers. Rides go within Putnam County and to certain places outside it.

library.name: Desmond-Fish Public Library
library.notes: Open Monday, Wednesday, Friday and Saturday 10 am to 5 pm, Tuesday and Thursday 10 am to 8 pm, and Sunday 1 to 5 pm.

more.name: Philipstown outreach (Office for Senior Resources)
more.note: Outreach staff help isolated older residents get services and apply or recertify for Medicaid, SNAP and the Medicare Savings Program.

more.name: Putnam County Office for Senior Resources
more.note: Main line for NY Connects, HIICAP Medicare counseling, EPIC help, home care, home delivered meals, caregiver support and a legal consultation with an attorney by appointment. name: Piermont
intro: Piermont is a small village on the Hudson River in the Town of Orangetown, with Village Hall at 478 Piermont Avenue. The Piermont Public Library is at Flywheel Park, an Orangetown senior club meets in the village, and the nearest Meals on Wheels senior center with lunch is in Tappan.

seniorCenter.name: Orangetown Senior Activity Center (Meals on Wheels Rockland)
seniorCenter.address: Tappan Reformed Church, 35 Kings Highway, Tappan, NY 10983
seniorCenter.notes: Free to join for Rockland residents 60 and older. Open Monday to Friday, 10 am to 2 pm, and closed on holidays and bad weather days. Lunch is made daily, with kosher, therapeutic and mechanically altered choices. The suggested donation is $4 for lunch and $2 for a ride, and no one is refused service for not giving. Call or fill out the center's online form to join.

transport.name: TRIPS Paratransit (Rockland County)
transport.notes: A shared-ride bus for Rockland residents 60 and older, and for people with disabilities, who find the regular buses hard or impossible to use. Regular TRIPS runs 7 am to 7 pm Monday to Friday, with limited Saturday service from 8 am to 5 pm. For help with an application, the county lists 845-364-2065.

more.name: Village of Piermont, Village Hall
more.note: 478 Piermont Avenue, Piermont.

more.name: Orangetown Piermont senior club
more.note: Meets at St. John's Church, 895 Piermont Avenue, on the 2nd and 4th Wednesday at 1:30 pm. The phone is Orangetown Town Hall.

places.name: Tallman Mountain State Park
places.note: On Route 9W in Sparkill, open year round, dawn to dusk, with a walking trail and picnic areas. An $8 vehicle fee is collected on weekends and holidays from Memorial Day weekend to Columbus Day.

name: Port Chester
intro: Port Chester is a village in Westchester County. Its Senior Community Center on Grace Church Street is open to all Port Chester residents 60 and older, with no income rule or membership fee, and serves lunch at noon plus home-delivered meals.

seniorCenter.name: Port Chester Senior Community Center
seniorCenter.address: 222 Grace Church Street, Port Chester, NY 10573
seniorCenter.notes: Open Monday to Friday, 9 am to 4 pm; Saturday hours (normally 9 am to 3 pm) are temporarily suspended through December 2026, and Saturday meals are handed out as take-home meals on Fridays. Lunch is served at noon, with a suggested contribution of $2 for residents and $4 for nonresidents; no one is turned away. The center has a library, computer room and pool table, with Zumba, tai chi, bridge, mah-jongg, bingo, art classes, day trips and movies. Medically homebound village seniors may get home-delivered meals on weekdays ($2 suggested).

transport.name: Port Chester Senior Community Center transportation
transport.notes: The center provides rides for village residents. Call for details. Bee-Line ParaTransit (914-995-7272) serves people who cannot ride regular buses, for a $5 fare.

intro: Port Jervis is a city in Orange County. The city runs a Dial-A-Ride bus with a 50 cent senior fare that also reaches a few miles into the Town of Deerpark, and the Port Jervis Free Library is on Pike Street.

transport.name: City of Port Jervis Dial-A-Ride
transport.notes: Rides within the city limits and up to 3 miles into the Town of Deerpark. The bus runs Monday to Friday 6 am to 3:30 pm. The senior fare is $0.50. Call 8 am to 1 pm on weekdays, by noon the business day before your ride (by Friday noon for a Monday ride).

library.name: Port Jervis Free Library
library.notes: Open Monday, Tuesday and Thursday 10 am to 9 pm, Wednesday and Friday 10 am to 6 pm and Saturday 10 am to 5 pm. Closed Sunday.

more.name: Orange County Office for the Aging
more.note: Aging Services Specialists answer questions about county services for older adults and can arrange home visits for homebound seniors. Bilingual help is available.

name: Port Richmond
intro: Port Richmond is a Staten Island neighborhood. Catholic Charities of Staten Island runs the Anderson Older Adult Center here under contract with NYC Aging. The Port Richmond Library, a Carnegie branch from 1905, faces Veterans Park on Bennett Street.

seniorCenter.name: Anderson Older Adult Center (Catholic Charities of Staten Island)
seniorCenter.address: 120 Anderson Avenue, Port Richmond, Staten Island, NY 10302
seniorCenter.notes: Open Monday to Friday, 7 am to 3 pm. Membership is free for adults 60 and older, and members may come as often as they like. The center serves fresh meals and offers exercise and wellness programs, trips and social service support. Transportation is available to members based on eligibility and availability. Funded under contract with NYC Aging.

transport.name: Access-A-Ride (MTA paratransit)
transport.notes: Shared-ride service for people whose disabilities keep them from using buses or the subway. It runs 24 hours a day, every day, including holidays, in all five boroughs. The fare is the same as the full subway and bus fare, paid in exact change, and an authorized personal care attendant rides free. Press 2 to book a trip one to two days ahead (agents 7 am to 5 pm, every day), or press 4 for eligibility and application questions (9 am to 5 pm, Monday to Friday). Anyone 65 or older can also get the MTA Reduced Fare, $1.50 a ride on the subway, local buses and the Staten Island Railway.

library.name: Port Richmond Library
library.notes: Fully accessible. The branch keeps its fireplaces, oak shelving and original furniture and offers free programs. Check the branch page for this week's hours. The New York Public Library no longer charges late fines.

more.name: NY Connects Staten Island (Community Agency for Senior Citizens)
more.note: Free help finding home care, caregiver support, home delivered meals, transportation, health insurance and help applying for benefits. intro: Pound Ridge is a town in Westchester County. Its Neighbor to Neighbor program, run by volunteers with the town Recreation and Police departments, helps older and disabled residents with rides to doctors and food shopping, hot meals when someone cannot cook, a reassurance call program and a medical equipment loan closet.

seniorCenter.notes: A community volunteer program working with the Town Recreation Department and Police Department. Services include rides to doctors and to food shopping at The Market at Pound Ridge Square, volunteers who shop for you if you cannot get out, hot meals delivered when you are temporarily unable to cook, senior social events, the Call Reassurance program, File of Life and a medical equipment loan program. The program is reached through the town's Adults 62+ coordinator at the Town House.

transport.name: Neighbor to Neighbor rides
transport.notes: Volunteer rides to doctors and to food shopping. Call to arrange. Bee-Line ParaTransit (914-995-7272) serves people who cannot ride regular buses.

intro: Rye is a city in Westchester County. Rye Recreation runs a Senior Adult Program for City of Rye residents 60 and older at the Damiano Recreation Center, with exercise classes, luncheons, speakers and trips.

seniorCenter.name: Rye Seniors (Rye Recreation Senior Adult Program)
seniorCenter.address: Damiano Recreation Center, 281 Midland Avenue, Rye, NY 10580
seniorCenter.notes: Open to all City of Rye residents 60 and older. Members gather for exercise, strength and balance classes, Zumba Gold, Pilates, painting, crafts, games, luncheons and movies, with monthly speakers and shopping, theater and lunch trips. Advance registration is required for all programs and events. Email ryeseniors@ryeny.gov.

transport.notes: County shared-ride, curb to curb service for people who cannot ride regular Bee-Line buses. It runs within 3/4 mile of a Bee-Line bus route, during the hours that route runs. Book Monday to Friday, 9 am to 5 pm, up to 7 days ahead; next-day trips must be booked by 5 pm. You must apply and be found eligible first (press 3 on the phone line for an application).

library.notes: Open Monday to Thursday 9:30 am to 8 pm, Friday 9:30 am to 5:30 pm, Saturday 10 am to 5 pm and Sunday noon to 5 pm.

name: Scarsdale
intro: Scarsdale is both a town and a village in Westchester County. Residents 60 and older can join the Scarsdale Seniors Club for exercise classes, summer aqua aerobics and reduced rates on trips and programs, and village members can get taxi vouchers for nearby medical visits. A free daily check-in call runs with the Scarsdale Police Department.

seniorCenter.name: Scarsdale Seniors Club (Village of Scarsdale)
seniorCenter.notes: Open to Scarsdale residents 60 and older. The club offers exercise classes, aqua aerobics in summer, and special rates for tennis permits, trips and programs. Call the senior citizen coordinator or register online through the village. The village also runs a free daily phone check-in with the Scarsdale Police Department, called Are You OK (RUOK). If no one answers after three calls, police go to the home. Call the police non-emergency line to sign up.

transport.name: Scarsdale Seniors medical taxi vouchers
transport.notes: Scarsdale Seniors Club members who live in the village can get a taxi voucher for local medical and dental appointments, preferably between 10 am and 2 pm. Call at least one week ahead; the voucher covers one way of the trip. Bee-Line ParaTransit (914-995-7272) serves people who cannot ride regular buses, for a $5 fare.

more.name: Scarsdale Edgemont Family Counseling Service, Aging in Place program
more.note: A joint effort of the Village of Scarsdale and this nonprofit at 14 Harwood Court, Suite 409. It offers in-home counseling and assessment for homebound residents, home safety checks, information and referral to vetted providers, advocacy and help planning for the future.

more.name: Eastchester Garth Road Senior Center
more.note: A Town of Eastchester neighborhood center at 235 Garth Road with a Scarsdale address, open Wednesday and Friday afternoons for residents of that area.

name: Walden
intro: Walden is a village in the Town of Montgomery, with Village Hall at 1 Municipal Square. Older residents can ride the Town of Montgomery's free Senior Bus, get county home delivered meals, and use the Josephine-Louise Public Library.

transport.name: Town of Montgomery Senior Bus and Dial-A-Bus
transport.notes: Serves Walden along with the rest of the towns of Montgomery and Crawford. The Senior Bus is free for people 60 and older (donations encouraged), with monthly out-of-town trips and two medical runs a month to Middletown. Seniors can also ride the public Dial-A-Bus for $0.50. Call 9 am to noon on weekdays, at least a day ahead.

library.name: Josephine-Louise Public Library
library.notes: Open Monday to Thursday 10 am to 8 pm, Friday 10 am to 6 pm and Saturday 10 am to 2 pm; closed Sunday. Cards go to Village of Walden residents and Town of Montgomery residents with a Walden mailing address.

more.name: Montgomery Senior Center (county Senior Dining site)
more.note: The county senior lunch site at 36 Bridge Street in the Village of Montgomery, for people 60 and older. Reserve 24 hours ahead.

more.name: Village of Walden
more.note: Village Hall is open Monday to Thursday 7:30 am to 4:30 pm and Friday 8 am to noon. Parks and Recreation is ext. 1524.

more.name: Town of Montgomery Assessor
more.note: Call to see if you qualify for the senior (aged) and Enhanced STAR property tax exemptions.

name: Wallkill
intro: Wallkill is a town in Orange County next to the City of Middletown, with town offices at 99 Tower Drive. Local senior groups meet at the town Community Center on Wes Warren Drive, and the town Dial-A-Bus gives riders 60 and older a $1 fare anywhere in the town outside the city.

seniorCenter.name: Town of Wallkill Community Center (senior groups)
seniorCenter.notes: Local senior groups meet here regularly, along with a quilting club. The center is just off Route 211. Call the center Mondays, Tuesdays or Thursdays for details.

transport.name: Town of Wallkill Dial-A-Bus
transport.notes: Shared rides to and from places in the Town of Wallkill outside the City of Middletown. Buses run Monday to Friday 7:30 am to 5 pm and Saturday 8 am to 3:15 pm. The fare is $1 for riders 60 and older, disabled riders and Medicare card holders. Book by phone 8 am to 2 pm on weekdays, or online; booking several days ahead is advised, and Monday rides must be booked by 1 pm Friday. Tell the dispatcher if you need the wheelchair lift. No service on major holidays.

library.name: Middletown Thrall Library
library.notes: The public library in neighboring Middletown.

name: Warwick
intro: Warwick is a town in Orange County that takes in the villages of Warwick, Greenwood Lake and most of Florida, plus the hamlet of Pine Island. Senior clubs for people 55 and older meet across the town, two of them at the Warwick Senior Center behind Town Hall. The town Dial-A-Ride and village shuttle bus give a half fare to riders 60 and older.

seniorCenter.name: Warwick Senior Center (Town Hall complex)
seniorCenter.notes: The center sits behind Town Hall. Two town senior clubs for people 55 and older meet here. Warwick Valley Seniors meets every Wednesday at noon and Warwick Golden Senior Citizens meets every Thursday at 11:30 am. Other town clubs meet in Florida, Greenwood Lake and Pine Island. New members are welcome; attend a meeting to join.

transport.name: Town of Warwick Dial-A-Ride
transport.notes: Curb-to-curb rides Monday to Friday 8 am to 4:30 pm across the town, the villages of Florida and Greenwood Lake and the hamlet of Pine Island. Call 8 am to 2 pm on weekdays, at least 24 hours and up to one week ahead. The fare is $1 for riders 60 and older, disabled riders and Medicare card holders (proof needed), exact change. A village shuttle runs on a set route seven days a week with no reservation, and the bus also makes trips to Goshen, Monroe and Harriman, and Middletown shopping and medical centers on set days. The bus cannot use driveways or private roads, and drivers cannot help riders once they are off the bus.

library.name: Albert Wisner Public Library
library.notes: Open Monday to Thursday 9 am to 8 pm, Friday 9 am to 5 pm, Saturday 10 am to 5 pm and Sunday noon to 4 pm. For curbside pickup or homebound delivery, call and choose option 3. Homebound service, by mail or delivery, is open to cardholders who cannot get to the library.

more.name: NJ Transit buses 196 and 197
more.note: The town notes these buses run from Warwick to New York City, with stops in the town and the villages of Warwick and Greenwood Lake and a free Park and Ride lot on Route 17A.

name: Washingtonville
intro: Washingtonville is a village in the Town of Blooming Grove. Older residents use the town's Senior and Nutrition Center and its senior bus, which serves residents over 60 in the village, and the Moffat Library is on West Main Street with a drive-thru window and home delivery.

seniorCenter.name: Blooming Grove Senior and Nutrition Center
seniorCenter.notes: Lunch is served at noon three days a week for people 60 and older, including Tuesdays and Fridays. Call ahead to reserve and to confirm the days. There is no fee, and a $3.50 contribution per meal is suggested. Activities include a painting club, movies, mahjong, cards and bingo.

transport.name: Blooming Grove Senior Bus
transport.notes: Home pickup for town residents over 60, including Washingtonville. Wednesdays and Fridays go to Monroe area stores and Woodbury Commons, and Thursdays to Vails Gate and Newburgh shopping. A $1 donation is requested each way. Call at least 24 hours ahead, Monday to Friday.

library.name: Moffat Library of Washingtonville
library.notes: The library and its drive-thru window are open Monday to Thursday 10 am to 8 pm, Friday 10 am to 6 pm, Saturday 10 am to 5 pm and Sunday noon to 5 pm. The library has a home delivery service.

seniorCenter.notes: Open Monday to Friday, 8 am to 4 pm. Membership is free for adults 60 and older, and members may come as often as they like. intro: West Haverstraw is a village in the Town of Haverstraw, with Village Hall at 130 Samsondale Avenue. The Haverstraw King's Daughters Public Library's main building is in Garnerville, and the Meals on Wheels Haverstraw Senior Activity Center serves a weekday lunch on Hudson Avenue in Haverstraw.

seniorCenter.name: Haverstraw Senior Activity Center (Meals on Wheels Rockland)
seniorCenter.notes: Free to join for Rockland residents 60 and older. Open Monday to Friday, 10 am to 2 pm, and closed on holidays and bad weather days. Lunch is made daily, with kosher, therapeutic and mechanically altered choices. The suggested donation is $4 for lunch and $2 for a ride, and no one is refused service for not giving. Call or fill out the center's online form to join.

transport.name: TRIPS Paratransit (Rockland County)
transport.notes: A shared-ride bus for Rockland residents 60 and older, and for people with disabilities, who find the regular buses hard or impossible to use. Regular TRIPS runs 7 am to 7 pm Monday to Friday, with limited Saturday service from 8 am to 5 pm. For help with an application, the county lists 845-364-2065.

library.name: Haverstraw King's Daughters Public Library
library.notes: This is the main library. The Village Branch is at 85 Main Street in Haverstraw, 845-429-3445.

intro: West Nyack is a hamlet in the Town of Clarkstown. Two Clarkstown senior clubs meet at St. Francis of Assisi on Parrot Road, the Meals on Wheels lunch center is close by in Nanuet, and the West Nyack Free Library is on Strawtown Road.

seniorCenter.name: Clarkstown senior clubs at St. Francis of Assisi
seniorCenter.notes: The West Nyack I club meets Mondays, 1 to 4 pm, and the Upper Nyack club Wednesdays, noon to 3 pm, for Clarkstown residents 55 and older. The phone is the town's main line.

transport.name: Clarkstown Mini Trans
transport.notes: The town bus runs five routes that all meet at the Nanuet Mall. It runs Monday to Friday 6:55 am to 8:05 pm and Saturday 9 am to 7:10 pm, with no Sunday service. The senior and disabled fare is $0.40. It also gives weekday door-to-door rides to the Clarkstown senior clubs and rides from senior complexes to local supermarkets.

library.notes: The library lists a homebound delivery service.

name: White Plains
intro: White Plains is a city in Westchester County and the county seat. The city's Recreation and Parks Community Center on Mitchell Place runs programs for older adults, and the county lists it as a weekday lunch site for people 60 and older. Greenburgh's Theodore D. Young Community Center, with a White Plains address, serves lunch too.

seniorCenter.name: White Plains Community Center (Recreation and Parks)
seniorCenter.notes: The office is open Monday to Friday, 8:30 am to 4:30 pm. The county lists the center as a congregate lunch site for people 60 and older; register before your first meal, and the suggested contribution is voluntary. Call the center for the current senior program schedule.

transport.name: Bee-Line ParaTransit (Westchester County)
transport.notes: County shared-ride, curb to curb service for people who cannot ride regular Bee-Line buses. It runs within 3/4 mile of a Bee-Line bus route, during the hours that route runs. The fare is $5 a trip, paid in exact cash or with a ticket, and a personal care attendant listed on the rider's ID card rides free. Book Monday to Friday, 9 am to 5 pm, up to 7 days ahead; next-day trips must be booked by 5 pm. You must apply and be found eligible first (press 3 on the phone line for an application).

library.name: White Plains Public Library
library.notes: The library posted that it will have new hours of operation starting December 7, 2026, so check its website before you go. You can also text WPPL to 66746.

more.name: Westchester County Office for People with Disabilities
more.note: At 148 Martine Avenue in White Plains. Listed by the county for ParaTransit questions.

name: Woodbury
intro: Woodbury is a town in Orange County. The Woodbury Senior Center in Highland Mills serves older residents of Central Valley, Highland Mills and parts of Harriman, with walk-in hours most afternoons.

seniorCenter.name: Woodbury Senior Center
seniorCenter.notes: Walk-in hours are Monday to Thursday noon to 4 pm and Friday 10 am to 4 pm. Activities include movie matinees, weekly exercise classes, art socials, day trips, potlucks, concerts and a vegetable garden, plus guest speakers. A second center line is 845-928-5466. Stop in or call for the monthly calendar.

more.name: Orange County Office for the Aging
more.note: The senior center resource list points to the county aging office. Aging Services Specialists answer questions about county services for older adults and can arrange home visits for homebound seniors. Bilingual help is available.

name: Yonkers
intro: Yonkers is a city in Westchester County. The city's Office for the Aging works out of the Peter Chema Center on Riverdale Avenue, and the county lists five places in Yonkers that serve lunch to people 60 and older. Yonkers Public Library runs three branches and a 55+ events track.

seniorCenter.name: Yonkers Office for the Aging (Peter Chema Center)
seniorCenter.notes: The Peter Chema Senior Nutrition Center in the same building serves lunch and home-delivered meals for people 60 and older (nutrition line 914-963-6662). The county also lists lunch at the Scotti Center (680 Bronx River Road, 914-377-6490), Nepperhan Community Center (342 Warburton Avenue, 914-965-0203), North Yonkers Preservation and Development (219 Ridge Avenue, 914-522-0364) and the YWCA (87 South Broadway, 914-963-0640). You must register before your first meal, and the suggested contribution is voluntary.

transport.name: Bee-Line ParaTransit (Westchester County)
transport.notes: County shared-ride, curb to curb service for people who cannot ride regular Bee-Line buses. It runs within 3/4 mile of a Bee-Line bus route, during the hours that route runs. The fare is $5 a trip, paid in exact cash or with a ticket, and a personal care attendant listed on the rider's ID card rides free. Book Monday to Friday, 9 am to 5 pm, up to 7 days ahead; next-day trips must be booked by 5 pm. You must apply and be found eligible first (press 3 on the phone line for an application).

library.name: Yonkers Public Library
library.notes: It has three branches, the Riverfront Library, Grinton I. Will Library and Crestwood Library. Events are tagged for Adults 55+. A food pantry at the Riverfront Library is open Monday to Friday, 11 am to 3 pm, while supplies last (ext. 427 or 428).

more.name: Livable Community Connection (Yonkers Office for the Aging)
more.note: A program of the Office for the Aging at 435 Riverdale Avenue that connects Yonkers residents with services and resources to help them age in place.

more.name: Coyne Park Senior Center
more.note: Listed by the county at 777 McLean Avenue. The county's Yonkers list has more than 20 senior clubs and centers across the city.

name: Yorktown
intro: Yorktown is a town in Westchester County. Its senior services work out of the Albert A. Capellini Community and Cultural Center on Commerce Street, with a weekday hot lunch, home meals, a senior bus and weekly blood pressure checks.

seniorCenter.name: Yorktown Senior Nutrition Center (Albert A. Capellini Community and Cultural Center)
seniorCenter.notes: Open Monday to Friday, 9 am to 2:30 pm. Hot lunch is served weekdays at noon; reserve at least one day ahead by 1 pm. Hot meals are delivered weekdays to eligible homebound seniors. There is a suggested contribution. Blood pressure screening is weekly and sugar screening is the second Wednesday of the month, and Emergency Medical Door Bags are available at the center. Senior groups meet in the building; to join one, call Parks and Recreation at 914-245-4650.

transport.name: Yorktown Senior Services bus
transport.notes: Weekday rides to and from the Senior Nutrition Program and to local supermarkets, plus special holiday shopping outings. There is a suggested contribution. For other trips, Bee-Line ParaTransit (914-995-7272) serves people who cannot ride regular buses, for a $5 fare.
